_note: English renderings of the opening of Lucas's 1835 descriptions, abridged to two or three sentences. Keyed by the text entry's specimen id (plate + page-order figure). Entries under _mismatch carry a description that belongs to a different species than the index name: the parser's alignment was weak there.

_mismatch.n146-3: Text describes Papilio Plexippus (a Danais), not the indexed Leucippe.
_mismatch.n162-1: Text describes Colias Elathea, not Proterpia.
_mismatch.n164-1: Text describes Papilio Amathea (Vanessa amathea), not Elathea.
_mismatch.n214-2: Index gives Laomédia; text is Acraea Euryta.
_mismatch.n280-2: Text describes Papilio Salmasis, not Amasia.
_mismatch.n288-2: Text compares Demodice with Demophon; heading garbled.

n16-1: This butterfly, remarkable for the beauty of its colours and for its size, is without doubt one of the finest of its genus, and it was to this species that Linnaeus gave the epithet of Augustus. The forewings are oval, entire, of a matt velvet black above, with two bands of golden green, curved and narrow, one running along the costa and the other along the whole of the opposite edge.
n20-1: The forewings are velvet black above, with a patch of azure blue that turns violet or green according to the angle at which one examines it. This patch runs from the base of all four wings to beyond the middle, its hind edge scalloped, and near the front edge of the forewings there is a fairly large black dot, present in the female too.
n40-1: All the wings are toothed, black, with whitish notches. The forewings carry a whitish, interrupted streak opposite the apex; the hindwings are crossed in the middle by a broad greyish-white band, sinuous on its outer side, ending at the anal angle in a blood-red lunule dusted with blue.
n50-2: The four wings are toothed, of a deep blackish brown above, with whitish notches. Towards the middle of the wing the male shows a large patch of fine blue-green, set transversely and divided in three by the veins, and near the apex of the same wings three more spots of the same colour.
n56-1: This species, of middling size, is sulphur white on both surfaces. The tip of the forewings is edged above by a broad arched black band, much widened at the apex, where it carries a dot of the ground colour; the hindwings have very blunt teeth and a fairly long yellowish spatulate tail, with three black spots towards the middle of the surface.
n68-1: The wings are deep black above and crossed towards the middle by a band of greenish yellow, narrowed and broken into round spots near the apex of the forewings; the hindwings carry a row of lunules of the same colour parallel to the hind edge. These wings are very bluntly toothed, edged with white at the notches, and end in a black tail a little spatulate.
n86-1: This species of middling size is brownish black, with a yellow transverse band made up of triangular spots on the forewings and divided by black veins on the hindwings. The hind edge of the forewings is slightly toothed and preceded by a row of yellow dots; the hindwings have curved blunt teeth, a black tail of moderate length, and a tawny anal angle marked with a very black dot beneath a lunule of blue atoms.
n98-1: The wings are white above with a very faint greenish tint, gently strengthened at the base and apex of the forewings; along the costa run seven transverse black bands, the three foremost nearly equal, the next two short, the two hindmost longer and broader, ending in a point and meeting near the inner angle. The hindwings have their lower edge cut by black lunules, mostly on an ashen ground.
n98-2: The wings are black above, with an interrupted band, four transverse streaks and a row of marginal spots of pale green. The band curves inward and crosses the middle of all four wings; the streak nearest the body continues on the hindwings to above the anal angle, where it ends in a dot of carmine red.
n102-1: This is a large species; all its wings are slightly toothed, brownish black above, and crossed in the middle by a fairly broad white band faintly tinged with yellow, a little fringed on the hindwings and cut by fine black veins. The small notches of the forewings are edged with faintly yellowish dots, those of the hindwings with oblong spots of the same colour.
n102-2: This species closely resembles Zenobius, but is much smaller and much less dark in colour. All the wings are toothed and finely edged with white on both surfaces; the forewings are reddish brown, crossed in the middle by a broad band finely cut by reddish veins and strongly interrupted towards the front.
n112-1: The wings are nearly round, entire, of a frosted blue; the forewings have a black border, broadest at the apex and toothed inwardly near the base, and are lightly speckled with black, as are the veins. Beneath, the forewings are pearl grey, faintly yellow at the base, and near the base the hindwings carry silky, faintly bluish hairs.
n112-2: All the wings above, and the forewings beneath, are white, both surfaces ending in a fairly broad black border, curved on the hindwings and forming on the forewings a long triangle whose point reaches the inner angle. Beneath, the costa of the forewings is edged with black and washed with a yellow that fades from the border towards the base.
n114-1: All the wings are bluish white above, with the hind margin, the vein tips and the costa of the forewings black. The black band, broadest at the apex, is lightly toothed inwardly; the middle of the hindwings is white and faintly orange where the marigold-coloured patch beneath shows through.
n114-3: All the wings are white. The forewings carry at the apex an arched and widened patch, sometimes elliptical, sometimes joined into a continuous band, and their base is orange with a blackish costa. Beneath, the apex is paler and faintly greenish, the base a deeper orange spreading much further than above.
n116-2: The wings are white faintly tinged with blue above, with a dark base. The forewings have the whole costa black and, at the tip, a border of the same colour, sinuous inwardly and widened at the apex, where it is divided by a broken band or by two white spots. Beneath, the hindwings are entirely pearl grey with a faint violet gleam.
n116-3: The wings are white above with a dark base. The male has at the tip of the forewings a black border, sinuous inwardly and broader at the apex, where it shows a transverse row of five or six white triangular spots pointing outward; the hindwings are edged by a run of closely set oval black spots.
n118-1: The wings are white above, with a broad black hind border entirely divided by a row of white spots, the foremost oval, the rest round and smaller. The forewings also have, towards the middle of the costa, a curved transverse black band, broader in the female than in the male; beneath, the hindwings are strongly veined with black and marked with deep yellow.
n118-3: The wings are bluish white above in the male and yellow-tinged white in the female, with a black hind border sinuous on its inner side, very broad in the female. Both sexes are black beneath, with a very large orange patch at the base of the forewings and a transverse row of four or five oval greenish spots on the hind margin.
n128-3: The male is white above, with the hind margin of the hindwings and two thirds of the costa of the forewings black, the forewings also bearing at the tip a very large triangular black space. Beneath, the forewings are black with a whitish crescent in the middle; the hindwings are ochre yellow, with a fairly broad black border saw-toothed on its inner side.
n128-2: The forewings are white above, with the base and most of the costa ashen, the veins black and the middle one much widened, and at the tip a black border carrying four or five small oblong white spots. The hindwings above are a fine yellow, turning orange towards the anal angle, with the whole hind margin black.
n130-1: The male is bluish white above, with a black apex divided transversely by an arched band of four or five oval white spots, and a narrow black border to the hindwings. The female is dull white above with each wing broadly edged in black; both sexes are black beneath, with about the front third of all four wings yellow and pricked with blackish.
n130-2: The forewings are white above with a black apex divided transversely by an arched band of four or five white spots; the hindwings are faintly bluish above with a fairly broad black border cut by a run of whitish dots. Beneath, the hindwings are clouded yellow from base to middle, then black to the tip, with a marginal row of six marigold-coloured spots, three heart-shaped and three nearly round.
n130-3: Above, the male is bluish white with black veins, more pronounced on the forewings than the hindwings, and each wing ends in a broad black border faintly fringed with whitish, arched and gently sinuous inwardly. Along its whole length this border is divided by a row of fairly large oval spots, white on the forewings and faintly flesh-coloured on the hindwings.
n132-1: The male is a slightly bluish white above, with the hind margin of the hindwings black. The forewings end in a black band forming a long triangle, its inner side sinuous, cut along its length by a run of six whitish spots, the first five elliptical and larger, the sixth rounded. All four wings are entirely veined with black beneath.
n132-2: The wings are bluish white above, especially in the male. The forewings have the costa lightly edged with black and, at the tip, a large deep black triangular space, arched and faintly sinuous inwardly, divided opposite the apex by a transverse line of three or four small white spots. Both sexes are brownish black beneath, dusted with white, with a deep yellow oblique band at the apex of the forewings.
n132-3: The wings are bluish white above, broadly edged with black at their tips. The forewings carry at the apex an arched, spotted white band; the hindwings are unspotted. Beneath, both are velvet black with a whitish lunule in the middle, and the hindwings are crossed by a vermilion red band, spotted and winding, from the front edge to the inner edge.
n134-1: The wings are bluish white above with a very broad black hind border on which are ranged round spots close to the ground colour. Below the costa of the forewings, near this border, the male has a black space divided across by a white lunule; in the female this space merges with the border and shows, besides the lunule, an angular white band facing the apex.
n134-2: All the wings are white, with a light black border at the tip of the hindwings and along the costa of the forewings, which carry at the apex a triangular black space whose point rests on the middle of the hind edge. Beneath, the hindwings are brownish black with two transverse bands, the front one pale sulphur yellow, the hind one white washed with yellow, separated by a streak of marigold red.
n134-3: The four wings above are white faintly tinged with green. The forewings are edged at the tip by a very black band of moderate width forming a long triangle pointing downward, its inner side sinuous and cut by five or six small longitudinal black strokes; the hindwings are unspotted. Beneath, the black of the costa and tip is replaced by pale ochre yellow.
n144-2: The male is greenish white above with the veins and the hind margin black; the costa of the forewings is likewise black, and their tip shows a marginal row of whitish dots. In the female these dots appear on all four wings, the ground is less green and the veins are wider. Beneath, the hindwings are pearl grey with a faint violet gleam. This Pieris is found in the island of Java.
n146-3: The forewings above are a vivid tawny, lightly glazed with red, with a clouded greenish-yellow base and the veins and whole outer edge black; parallel to the hind edge runs a row of black triangular spots pointing towards the base, larger and closer in the female. The hindwings are a fine lemon yellow above, edged in the female by a black band toothed inwardly.
n146-2: The wings are a cheerful tawny above, with the veins black and widened; the hind margin is also black, with two rows of unequal white dots preceded outwardly by a small broken edging of the same colour. The forewings have at the apex a large triangular black space crossed obliquely by a fine white angular band made up of five touching spots.
n148-1: The male is bluish white above, the female yellowish white. In both sexes the forewings carry at the tip a very large triangular black space bearing a broad, arched patch of dawn orange, a little paler in the female and cut by a transverse line of black dots. The hindwings have the hind margin black in both sexes and the edge slightly sinuous.
n148-2: Both sexes are lemon yellow above. The forewings have at the tip a very large triangular black space on which sits an arched patch of dawn orange, narrowed at its lower end and a little paler in the female; the hindwings have a black hind margin. Beneath, all four wings are greenish yellow with usually only a very small blackish dot in the middle of each.
n148-3: The wings are lemon yellow above, with the margin of the hindwings and the rear half of the forewings black. The forewings also carry, opposite the apex, an oblique transverse band, yellow or pale dawn according to sex, sinuous on both sides and marked with a dot near its lower end. This species is found in China, in Bengal and in the island of Java.
n150-1: The forewings above are faintly ashen at the base, lemon yellow along the inner edge and black over the rest, with a very large patch of dawn orange rounded outwardly, marked with a black dot in its middle and divided by veins of that colour. The hindwings are lemon yellow above with a black border, sometimes very narrow, sometimes fairly broad, toothed on its inner side.
n150-2: All the wings are pale tawny above with a row of black dots along the hind edge. The forewings have a black dot in the middle and, between this and the marginal dots, a curved, broken transverse black streak that does not reach the inner edge. Beneath, the hindwings are very pale yellow with a faintly blackish waved streak continuing the streak of the forewings.
n150-4: The four wings are white above. The forewings have at the tip a triangular black space almost entirely filled by a patch of fine carmine red; the hindwings carry a run of black triangular spots along the hind edge. Beneath, the apex of the forewings is whitish with a narrow reddish band cut lengthwise by a line of black dots.
n160-1: The four wings are white above with a faintly dark base. The forewings have at the apex a fairly large triangular black space bearing a patch of vivid tawny, rounded outwardly, sinuous inwardly and a little narrowed at its lower end, and a very small black dot in the middle. The hindwings carry on the hind margin a row of nearly round black spots.
n160-2: The wings are white faintly tinged with yellow above, with a black base. The forewings have the apex black with a pale tawny patch rounded outwardly and deeply cleft, and a black dot in the middle, more or less distinct. The hindwings are broadly edged with black at the tip, with a broken row of fairly large white dots.
n160-4: The four wings are white, the base speckled with blackish. The forewings have at the tip an arched black border, narrow towards the inner angle and broad opposite the apex, where it is divided obliquely by a fine and very brilliant violet band, rounded outwardly; in the middle is a very black dot that repeats on the underside.
n162-1: The forewings are canary yellow with a black border fringed with whitish outwardly, faintly sinuous inwardly and ending in a point at the inner angle; in the male the costa is also broadly edged with black, and from the base runs a straight black line along almost the whole lower edge, which is orange. The hindwings are white above with a black border finely and irregularly toothed towards the base.
n162-3: The four wings are a fine deep yellow above, with a broad black border embracing their outline, a little narrower on the costa of the hindwings. Beneath, the border is a less deep black; the antennae are black, the body blackish above and yellow beneath, with a blackish line along the sides reaching the anal part. Found in the island of Amboina.
n162-2: The upperside of all four wings is a fine yellow. The forewings have at the tip a black border lightly edged with yellow outwardly and very sinuous inwardly, beginning in a point towards the middle of the costa and ending at the inner angle in a very broad hook; the hindwings have a narrower black border, arched and crenellated only on the side facing the base.
n162-4: The four wings are a vivid tawny above with a fairly broad black border, sinuous below, narrowed in the middle on the forewings and widened on the hindwings. The forewings also carry a black crescent in the middle. Beneath, the wings are paler and the border is replaced by blackish atoms; the hindwings are yellow with several rust-coloured spots.
n164-1: The wings are blackish brown above, with a broad transverse band of blood red across the disc, cleft at each end and not reaching the tip of the hindwings. On the forewings this band is preceded outwardly by a narrower white band of five touching spots, and near the hind edge of each wing runs a line of white dots.
n164-2: The male is a fine yellow above, the female a pale sulphur yellow, with a brownish-black border edged with reddish outwardly and sinuous inwardly, very narrow on the hindwings of the male and formed, on those of the female, by a run of spots of which the foremost is much the largest. Beneath, the forewings are yellow with a black dot in the middle.
n164-3: The upperside of the wings is a shining silvery green, ending on the forewings in a large triangular space of dark green and on the hindwings in a clouded band carrying a row of black dots. Beneath, all four wings are meadow green with a few rusty spots in the middle and light silvery shades along the inner edge. Found on the west coast of Africa.
n164-4: The wings are canary yellow above, with a fairly broad black border divided, on the forewings of the female, by a strongly interrupted yellow spotted band. The forewings have an oblong black dot towards the middle of the costa; the hindwings have a pale, rounded orange patch on the disc, and beneath two silver dots, the outer one smaller.
n164-5: All the wings are a fine yellow above. The forewings, whose apex is a little sharp, have the front half of the costa dark, a fairly large black dot in the middle, and at the tip a very broad black border whose inner side is sinuous and deeply notched in the middle, its outer side finely cut with yellow and red-brown. The hindwings are rounded and marked in the middle with two orange dots.
n174-3: The wings are an orange yellow, a little shot with colour, above. Beneath, they are a deep ochre yellow, with silvery discal dots and winding reddish lines accompanied by a multitude of rusty atoms; in some individuals the silver dots have little brilliance. This species is found in Guiana and Brazil.
n174-2: The four wings are a shining greenish white; the forewings are lightly edged with black, and the lemon yellow of the upperside reaches the middle of the forewings and the margin of the hindwings. All four wings are greenish beneath; the body is greenish white, the antennae black with a whitish club.
n176-1: The upperside of all four wings is a fine lemon yellow, a little matt towards the tip. Beneath, they are greenish or greyish and shining, with a rusty line running from the apex of the forewings towards the middle of the inner edge of the hindwings. The body is lemon yellow above and faintly yellowish white beneath. This species is found in Guiana and Brazil.
n176-2: The wings are a vivid lemon yellow, a little matt towards the tip, and almost rounded in shape. The forewings have towards the middle a transverse orange patch of varying size; the hindwings are orange, sometimes from the middle to the tip, sometimes only at the tip, and the hind edge of both is cut by very small black dots.
n178-1: The wings are entire and greenish white. The upperside of the forewings shows at the slightly pointed apex a fine triangular patch of dawn orange running from the middle of the costa to the middle of the hind edge, bordered outwardly by a black line and marked on its inner side by a large black dot. Beneath, all the wings are greenish white with a rusty, faintly purplish patch near the centre.
n178-2: The wings are greenish white above with a central orange dot having a black pupil. The forewings also carry, towards the middle of the costa, a large patch of lemon yellow. Beneath, the wings are greenish and faintly netted, with a flesh-coloured central dot answering the eye-spot of the opposite surface. This species is found in Brazil.
n180-1: In the male the wings are white on both surfaces, with the base tawny and the tip black; the tip of the forewings shows above a run of small white strokes. Beneath, the hindwings carry towards the hind edge some twenty silver spots, the three at each end elongated on a white ground, the others round on a rusty ground, all edged with black.
n180-2: The wings are black above with an orange band, more or less narrow. On the forewings the band descends obliquely from the middle of the costa to the inner angle, where it bends a little; on the hindwings it is arched outwardly and runs from the apex to the anal angle, near which is an oblong red dot. Beneath, the space between base and band shows a multitude of small pale ochre dots.
n180-3: The four wings are a shining carmine red, with the outer margin and the costa of the forewings black. The black of the costa shows three unequal teeth above and reaches beyond the middle of the surface beneath; the hindwings often have a small black lunule at their centre. The body is red above and yellowish beneath. This species is found in Guiana and Brazil.
n182-1: The four wings are a greenish violet blue, changing to violet, with the whole costa and the apex of the forewings black. Beneath, they are lilac or pale shining violet, with seven or eight black dots ringed with whitish scattered over the middle of each wing; the anal region of the hindwings is greenish blue with two short white bands. The tails are black tipped with white.
n182-2: The four wings are a shining cornflower blue above with a black apex; the forewings of the male have a greyish eye-spot towards the middle of the costa. Beneath, they are dark brown with the origin of the costa red on all four wings; the hindwings carry a white, waved, broken transverse line edged with black on its inner side, and two black eye-spots. Found in Guiana and Brazil.
n182-4: The male is a deep velvet violet above, with the channel of the hindwings blackish. Beneath, the wings are blackish brown netted with grey, with a run of three golden-green rings on the middle of the forewings and a small band of atoms of the same green at the anal angle of the hindwings, ending in a large black dot. The tail is black with a white tip. This species is found in the East Indies.
n182-3: In the male the wings are a shining cornflower blue above, in the female a pale violet blue, with the apex of the forewings and the outer edge of the hindwings brownish black. Both sexes are a whitish satin grey beneath with a waved line of small black arcs, and the hindwings have at the anal angle two black eyes with a tawny iris, separated by a cluster of silvery blue atoms. This species is found in Bengal.
n184-2: The forewings are velvet black above, with a shot gleam from violet blue to azure according to the light; their front half is unspotted, the rest carries a great many white dots, the outer ones smaller and ranged along the edge. The hindwings above are brownish black, matt ash grey towards the apex; beneath, they show a dozen small violet spots between the middle and the apex.
n194-1: The forewings are black on both surfaces and crossed between the middle and the tip by a fairly broad white band, sinuous on its sides and cut by fine veins of the ground colour, preceded outwardly by one or two white dots and inwardly by four or five more. The hindwings above are brownish black with a white patch set transversely at the base.
n196-2: The wings are black above and dark brown beneath. The forewings carry on their front half three longitudinal spots of shining greenish yellow, two converging at the base and enclosing the third, which is much shorter; opposite the apex is a transparent transverse band faintly tinged with yellow, followed by white dots in two lines parallel to the hind edge.
n196-1: The ground of the forewings is black, and at the base is a large longitudinal tawny patch divided unequally in three by a forked black vein; opposite the apex is a white, spotted transverse band preceded outwardly by two marginal lines of white dots. The hindwings are brownish black with two rows of white dots on the hind margin and eight longitudinal white streaks running to the base.
n198-1: All the wings are elliptical, entire and a little transparent. Their upperside is greyish white with black veins and a black hind border, fairly broad, very sinuous on its inner side and divided across its whole width, at least on the forewings, by a run of large white dots, some round, some oval; between each vein, towards the tip, is a black lance-shaped spot reaching the border.
n200-2: All the wings are a fairly deep black above. The forewings carry in the middle a broad transverse band of dull minium red, a little oblique, ending almost in a point below and more sinuous in the female than in the male; the hindwings are unspotted. Beneath, the hindwings are brownish black with the front half of the costa dull sulphur yellow and a few blood-red dots ranged in a half circle against the base.
n200-1: The four wings are deep black above with a blue gleam at the base. The forewings have two oblique transverse patches of sulphur yellow, one in the middle and one near the apex, the latter very narrow and made of four touching spots; the hindwings are unspotted above, their hind edge a little toothed and finely edged with white at the notches.
n200-3: Between the middle and the apex the forewings carry a broad transverse band of more or less vivid vermilion red starting from the costa, with a single tooth outwardly near its lower end and not reaching the inner edge; at the base is a longitudinal yellow line ending in a dot. The hindwings have near their origin a straight band of sulphur yellow of moderate width.
n202-1: All the wings are black with bands of sulphur yellow. The forewings have three, the two outer ones transverse and oblique, the inner running straight from the base to the middle of the surface, where it bends a little to reach the hind edge; the hindwings have two transverse bands, the upper broad, straight and continuous, the lower curved and made of dots.
n202-2: The forewings are deep black with three faintly yellowish, transparent bands; the triangular patch at the base is the largest, while the transverse band across the middle is narrower and divided into five spots, the three lower ones dot-like. The hindwings are faintly yellowish and transparent, with widened veins and a black hind border, and four or five curved teeth.
n212-1: The upperside of all four wings is faintly yellowish. The forewings have at the apex a triangular black space on which sits a patch of fine pale tawny, rounded outwardly, sinuous inwardly and narrowed at its lower end; the hindwings carry a row of well-spaced black spots on the hind margin. The body is whitish beneath and black above.
n212-2: In this species the wings are proportionally less narrow than in the preceding ones. Their upperside is a deep matt black with the hind edge cut by white and slightly sinuous. The forewings are crossed by two lines of faintly shining sulphur-yellow spots, the inner line of about six spots arching from the middle of the costa towards the inner angle, the outer of four spots midway to the apex.
n214-1: The upperside of the hindwings is dark brown at the base and along the hind edge, and crossed between these by a broad curved band of tawny or cherry red, toothed outwardly and marked in the middle with a few black dots; in the male this band just reaches the forewings, in the female it rises much higher and is divided into five oval spots.
n214-2: The forewings are blackish brown and crossed by a band, reddish white in the male and very white in the female, broader in her than in him, sinuous on its sides and cut by fine veins of the ground colour; it descends obliquely from the costa towards the hind angle, narrows greatly above it and folds inward to reach the inner edge. The hindwings are reddish in the male and reddish white in the female.
n214-3: The forewings are dark brown with ochre-yellow spots arranged thus: two longitudinal at the base, the front one shorter; two nearly round in the middle; five oblong, unequal and touching, forming a transverse band opposite the apex. The hindwings above are rust-coloured with rays or streaks and a dark brown marginal band.
n216-1: The forewings are black above, with the inner edge and two bands tawny: the front band runs from the base to about the middle of the surface, where it is deeply cleft, then descends curving and widening to near the anal angle; the outer band lies obliquely opposite the apex without reaching the edges. The hindwings are tawny above with black streaks and a broad, curved, crenellated black border.
n216-2: The male is a vivid tawny above; the female a light tawny, a little darkened towards the base of the forewings. These have a black, slightly concave hind edge, and their apex shows from that edge to the middle of the costa a large triangular black space mostly filled by an oblique tawny patch cleft behind. The hindwings are toothed and end in a fairly broad black border divided by a double row of dusky tawny spots.
n226-1: All the wings are toothed and black above. The forewings have two bands of celadon green, one longitudinal, one transverse: the first, from the base, is lance-shaped and reaches the disc, keeping nearer the front edge than the inner; the second, broader and strongly interrupted, is made of five unequal oblong spots, and the costa carries a line of three or four small whitish-green spots from its middle to the apex.
n226-3: The four wings are nearly round and toothed. Their upperside is velvet black with a violet gleam, and a broad terminal band of ochre yellow, repeated beneath, formed of closely set wedge-shaped spots. Beneath, each wing is rust-coloured and drawn thus: between base and middle, three transverse bands of greyish green cut lengthwise by black lines, then a series of small spots parallel to the terminal band.
n228-2: The four wings are finely toothed and edged with whitish at the notches. The upperside is a vivid tawny in the male, a dark and faintly greenish brick colour in the female, with a very broad brownish-black border arched inwardly. This border casts a faint violet gleam and is entirely divided by two curved parallel lines of white crescents facing one another by their convex sides.
n228-1: The wings are tawny above with a blackish terminal band divided by a run of whitish crescents concave outwardly. Opposite the apex of the forewings is a large triangular space of bluish black joined to the border, carrying an oblique, sinuous white transverse band separated from the crescents by an arc of four or five white dots. The border of the hindwings is preceded inwardly by two rows of black spots.
n230-1: The forewings are tawny above with about fifteen black spots: the foremost linear and set transversely beneath the costa, which is itself black; the next forming a zigzag transverse band across the middle; the rest round, smaller and ranged in a line parallel to the hind edge, which is covered by a fairly broad black band toothed inwardly and divided in the male by tawny lunules, in the female by white dots.
n230-2: The wings are yellowish tawny strewn with black spots above and end in a black border crenellated inwardly and carrying two rows of bluish lunules facing one another. Opposite the apex of the forewings is a large triangular bluish-black space crossed by an oblique, sinuous white band cut by the veins and marked below with two black dots. Daubenton called it the Leopard of China.
n232-1: The wings are dark brown above with a broad transverse band of greenish white set between the middle and the hind margin. On the forewings the band is a double row of spots, the inner ones smaller and crescent-shaped, the outer oval and each charged with a large black dot; on the hindwings it is continuous, preceded outwardly by a string of lunules, with two black eye-spots having a bluish pupil and a yellow iris.
n234-2: The wings are greenish black above, a little shot, and crossed in the middle and towards the tip by a pale arched blue band, divided on the hindwings by a line of black dots. Beneath, the male is dark black from the base to beyond the middle, then wood grey strongly waved with brown, with a sinuous, almost marginal line of ashen atoms and a dirty white dot on the disc of the hindwings. Found in China.
n234-3: Above, the wings are ash-coloured, a little reddish in the male, with three blackish, waved transverse lines towards the rear, between which runs a transverse row of eye-spots, six on the forewings and five on the hindwings, all but the two middle ones having the inner side of the pupil tawny; there are also some blackish waves near the origin of the front edge of the forewings.
n244-2: The wings are tawny above with a dark base and a curved, transverse hind row of six violet dots edged with black, much larger on the hindwings, whose middle shows a small black spot; the forewings have beneath the costa three short, parallel, slightly arched transverse bands of the same colour. Beneath, the wings are like the upperside but generally paler and a little pricked with blackish. Inhabits the Cape of Good Hope.
n244-3: This species differs from the one just described in that the origin of the costa of the forewings is brown instead of whitish; the eye at their inner angle is much larger and less round, flanked by two black dots inside the same iris; the upperside of the hindwings has no blue band but three lilac eyes, the front one larger and furnished with three white pupils.
n246-1: The wings above are a deep velvet black in the male and brownish black in the female, with two black eyes having violet-blue pupils and a reddish-tawny iris. The forewings, whose costa is whitish from its origin to the middle, have near the base four small oblique lines alternately tawny and bluish, and towards the tip three white streaks, the innermost broader and shorter.
n246-3: The wings are yellow inclining to tawny above, with all the edges black. This colour spreads broadly at the base of the hindwings and sets off a patch of violet or lapis blue, of much the same shape and size as in the preceding species. The forewings have at the apex, where the black widens entirely, two transverse yellowish streaks, the inner one shorter.
n248-1: The upperside of each wing is dark brown with two black eyes, their pupil bluish and their iris yellowish grey. These eyes are immediately preceded outwardly by a tawny line, more or less deep, itself preceded by a double waved marginal line of the same grey as the iris. The forewings have towards the origin of the costa two small tawny streaks edged with black, and between the two eyes an oblique band, sometimes white, sometimes reddish.
n248-2: All the wings are blackish brown with a violet gleam running from the base to beyond the disc. The forewings have seven or eight white dots, one cut in two near the middle of the costa, the others in two lines parallel to the hind edge. The hindwings are unspotted on both surfaces, but their underside, entirely glazed with violet, shows two dark, waved transverse lines. This species is found in South America.
n248-3: The wings are blackish brown on both surfaces, the outer edge of the forewings less deep. Parallel to that edge the hindwings carry a broad, curved, spotted band of vivid vermilion red, finely notched on its sides; beneath it appears again, but rosy white and a little narrower, accompanied by four red dots, three near the base and one towards the middle of the costa.
n250-1: The wings are brownish black above with a common, oblique tawny band across the disc. On the forewings the band is spotted, cleft in front and marked below the cleft with a line of three small black dots; on the hindwings it goes no further than the disc, and these wings have a reddish dot at the apex and a double row of unequal violet-blue dots along the outer edge.
n250-2: The wings are blue-black above with two transverse hind rows of light blue dots and a quite terminal row of earthy yellow lunules. Beneath, the ground of all four wings is a faintly shining greyish brown; towards the base are black, waved transverse strokes lightly edged with bluish, followed by a winding transverse series of yellowish dots.
n252-1: The wings are blackish brown above with a tawny or yellowish band towards the tip of the forewings and a white band towards the tip of the hindwings. The band of the forewings descends from the costa to the inner angle and is made of tawny dots in the male and of large wedge-shaped yellowish spots in the female. The marginal band of the hindwings is preceded by a band of ashen blue carrying a curved row of eight black eyes with bluish pupils.
n252-2: The wings are brownish black above, with the front half of the hindwings and a large triangular space at the origin of the inner edge of the forewings a livid yellow. The forewings have nine round spots of the same yellow, two a little beyond the middle of the costa and seven ranged parallel to the hind edge; the hindwings have two rows of blue lunules, the marginal one ending at the anal angle in a tawny crescent.
n262-1: In this species the tooth before the anal angle of the hindwings stands out more than the others, and in the female the end of the tail is shaped, so to speak, like a foot. The wings above are brownish black with a violet gleam, with a broad, sinuous band of pale ochre yellow descending from the middle of the costa to the inner angle of the forewings, which carry one or more dots of the same yellow at the apex.
n262-2: The wings are blackish brown above, crossed obliquely in the middle by a band of violet-tinged white, narrower on the forewings than the hindwings. The hindwings have the lower edge tawny from the anal angle to the tail inclusive, with five violet dots, the three outer ones edged with black. Beneath, all the wings are rusty brown with a few black, curved transverse lines edged with bluish at the base.
n264-1: Above, the front half of the wings is white, passing to yellowish towards the costa of the forewings; the other half is rusty, with two transverse rows of large tawny dots and an intermediate row of blackish dots on the forewings, and the reverse arrangement on the hindwings. Beneath, all the wings are the yellow of a dead leaf, with a few brown, waved transverse lines pricked with bluish near the base.
n266-1: The forewings are brownish black above with a longitudinal tawny band covering about the whole front third of the surface, then narrowing to end a little short of the hind edge; towards the tip of the front edge is an oval white spot set lengthwise. The hindwings are brownish black above with a dusky tawny edge. Beneath, all four wings are brown shaded with grey, with two darker transverse bands near the base.
n270-1: The wings are blackish brown above with a common, oblique white band across the disc, rounded at its front end and sharp or nearly so at the other. Opposite the apex the forewings carry an orange spot, more or less round in the male and an inverted triangle in the female, always separate from the white band; at the anal angle the hindwings have a small tawny patch bearing two black dots.
n270-3: Above, the wings are blackish brown with a common, oblique white band across the disc, less divided on the hindwings than on the forewings. The forewings have towards the origin of the costa three transverse spots of rusty red framed in black and separated by bluish ash; the hindwings have at the anal angle a tawny patch marked with two black dots. Beneath, two rusty lines with a white line between them run parallel to the outer edge.
n280-3: The wings are black above, with a common discal band whose inner side is mostly white and whose outer side is slate blue, spreading in rays to the hind edge. This edge carries white dots, the inner ones oblong and set in an arched line, the outer ones on the notches. Beneath, all four wings are dark brown with two rows of marginal dots as above and a band of violet-tinged white.
n280-2: The wings are a vermilion red, a little shot, above, with an almost terminal row of black dots, faint on the forewings and joined on the hindwings by an angular black line. Beneath, all four wings are a light tan brown with black hieroglyphs at the base, a common oblique rusty line across the middle and dark chevrons topped with violet dots at the tip. The body is brown above and yellowish beneath.
n282-1: The upperside of both sexes is a smoky black, crossed between the middle and the hind edge of the hindwings by a tawny band divided along its whole length by a curved row of seven very black oval spots, all, even the double and smaller anal one, carrying a blue dot in the middle. In the male this tawny band is narrower and surmounted by a large, faintly shining lilac patch. Daubenton called it the Palatine.
n282-2: The male is brownish black beneath, and shows towards the middle of each wing a white patch surrounded by a violet gleam and cut by the veins: round on the hindwings, oblong and oblique on the forewings, which carry a similar but much smaller patch at the apex. Lucas lists more than a dozen names under which earlier authors had described this variable species.
n284-1: Above, the wings are a shot black with a common, arched blue band across the disc, behind which run three strings of blue spots, the inner ones wedge-shaped, the outer lunulate and placed opposite the notches, which are edged with white on both surfaces. Beneath, the wings carry the same pattern, but the edge is brown, the band and spots bluish white, and the costa of the forewings is dotted and dusted with white near its origin.
n286-1: The four wings are black above; the forewings show two transverse bands of a deep colour inclining to reddish, the one at the base very broad, the one nearer the front narrower and rounded on its outer side. The hindwings have a single band of the same colour, narrow, a little sinuous on the inner side and rounded behind. Beneath, the forewings also show a narrow, slightly arched yellow band and a very narrow blue one.
n286-4: The wings are velvet black above with a shining orange band across the disc, a little curved and scarcely rising beyond the centre of the forewings. Beneath, the forewings are a shining blackish brown with the rear half of the costa violet grey and the disc yellowish and furnished with black hairs lying flat; the hindwings are brown faintly shaded with grey, with an arched transverse line of a few blackish dots. Daubenton called it the Velvet.
n286-3: The wings are black above with a violet-blue gleam, changing in the male and absent in the female. In both sexes the forewings have at the base a longitudinal line, in the middle a transverse band and at the apex an oblique dash of a green that looks more or less golden according to the light; the hindwings have a band of golden or bluish green along the outer edge. Beneath, the forewings are carmine red from their origin to beyond the middle.
n288-1: The wings are black above with a common, oblique band of shining greenish blue across the disc, arched and interrupted near the costa of the forewings and ending in a point on the hindwings. Beneath, the wings are brownish with three transverse bands of pearl grey, a black dot at the base of each wing and a waved line of the same colour descending from the front quarter of the costa to the inner angle.
n288-2: Both sexes of Nymphalis Demophon closely resemble the female of Nymphalis Demodice on the upperside; but the male of the latter has the blue band surrounded by a broad violet gleam, ending in a point a little beyond the disc of the forewings instead of being interrupted and arched near their upper edge. Beneath, rather more than the front half of all four wings is greyish white.
n300-1: The wings are black above with a common band of shining violet blue across the disc, which reaches almost to the root of the wings while losing its brilliance. The forewings have towards the middle of the costa an oblique white spot and towards the tip white dots in one row in the male and two in the female; the hindwings, whose notches are also white, carry a series of red dots along the hind edge.
n302-1: The male of this species had been given by authors under the name Menelaus, the female under that of Nestor. The upperside of the male's wings is a brilliant azure blue with the whole outer outline black and the notches of the outer edge yellowish white; on the costa of the forewings are three small white spots. The female is a somewhat less vivid blue, with the hind margin broadly black and charged with a row of white spots on the hindwings.
n304-1: The four wings are slightly toothed and a pearly white on both surfaces. Along the hind edge the upperside carries a double string of black spots, larger in the female, where they are separated by a scalloped black line; in both sexes the front half of the costa of the forewings is covered by a black streak that widens into a hook behind the submarginal cell. Beneath, a transverse row of black eyes with a tawny iris crosses the middle of the surface.
n306-1: The four wings above are velvet black, especially towards the base, with faint, slightly yellowish notches. The forewings carry a transverse band of fine blue that shines according to the light, much broader towards the base and divided in three by the veins; near the outer edge a longitudinal band of pale yellow crossed by black veins runs from the apex of the forewings to the anal angle of the hindwings.
n306-2: The wings are very entire and dark brown above. The forewings, whose front edge is strongly arched, are crossed from the middle of that edge by a curved, slightly sinuous tawny band reaching the inner angle and sometimes continuing, though shorter, to the corresponding angle of the hindwings; this band is more or less cleft at its origin. Beneath, all four wings are paler and finely pricked with grey, with a small black eye with a white pupil on the forewings.
n308-3: In this species the forewings are entire and a little transparent. Their upperside is dark brown, sometimes unspotted, sometimes carrying parallel to the hind edge a run of four or five dots, the second from the costa black in a grey ring, the others wholly bluish. The hindwings are a little toothed and end outwardly in a small blunt tail; their rear half is deep black with some twenty blue spots, most charged with a very white dot.
n310-1: The forewings are a little transparent, dark brown on both surfaces, with a linear white band descending obliquely from the end of the costa to the end of the inner edge. The upperside of the hindwings has about the front half and the outer edge dark brown, and all the rest tawny or Spanish-tobacco coloured, with a very white band edged with blackish; between this band and the hind edge are two very black eyes with bluish pupils.
n310-2: The body is a dusky blackish with a tint of silky green at the upper root of the wings. The transverse white line of the forewings is made of four or five spots, touching or merely separated by veins, and ends a little before the inner angle; the hindwings have four more white, diaphanous but very small spots, one adjoining the hind edge of the streak near its middle and three in a little line near the costa.
